howto.name: Upload WebP images
howto.text: Drop one or many .webp files, up to 100 images and 200 MB in total.

howto.name: Choose page size
howto.text: Auto (the default) makes each page the size of its image; A4 or Letter fit each image on a standard page. Transparency is not kept: transparent areas show the colour stored underneath, which is often black.

howto.name: Download the PDF
howto.text: All images become one PDF in upload order. The PDF is usually much larger than the WebP files, because the pixels are stored with lossless compression.

faq.q: Will the PDF be much smaller than from JPG?
faq.a: No, usually larger. WebP pixels are decoded and stored with lossless compression, so a lossy WebP photo can grow many times over, while a JPG is placed in the PDF without re-encoding.
Only the first frame is used. PDF doesn't support animation.

No. Only the colour of each pixel is stored, so transparent areas show whatever colour is stored beneath them, which is often black. Flatten the image onto a white background first if you need a white page.
